site.name: Orrery
footer.tagline: Orrery: everything that moves, in 102 colors. Built for NASA Space Apps 2026 from public SPHEREx images.
nav.label: Main
badge.data.help: Measured directly: pixels or catalogue values as recorded.
badge.model.help: Computed from a physical model, not measured.
badge.derived.help: Calculated from the data by our pipeline.
badge.resid.help: Data minus our model of the steady sky: what is left over.
home.lede: This asteroid is too faint to see in any one picture; slide to add more pictures along its path and watch it appear, with its colors.
reveal.caption: {n} of {N} pictures combined
reveal.snr: It stands out {snr} times above the noise.
reveal.no_spectrum: Add more pictures to start seeing its colors.
reveal.spec_title: Brightness of {object} at each color, from {n} pictures
reveal.gain: Combining all {N} pictures shows things about {x} times fainter than one picture can.
start.lede: One minute, a few steps. Press Next, or use the arrow keys.
start.title_timemachine: Most changes in raw blinking are only color
start.title_reveal: Faint movers appear when pictures are combined
start.title_object: Check our numbers against independent ones
tm.hint: The same patch of sky on different days. Anything that jumps or flickers changed. Use ← → to step.
tm.raw_explain: Raw: each picture was taken in a different infrared color, so stars seem to brighten and fade even when nothing changed.
tm.corrected_explain: Corrected: we remove what the steady sky should look like in each picture's color. What is left really changed.
tm.alt_raw: Raw picture of {name} on {date}, color {wl} µm
tm.alt_corr: Corrected change picture of {name} on {date}, color {wl} µm
objects.lede: Every asteroid we measured. Pick one to see its path, colors, size and the pictures behind each number.
obj.eta_check: This is a setting of the heat model, chosen to fit the infrared colors, not measured independently.
obj.spec_lede: How much sunlight it reflects at each color.
obj.check_gaia: Check it: show the independent Gaia spectrum
obj.sound_help: Plays 3 seconds: time goes from short to long wavelength; higher pitch means more light reflected.
obj.path_title: Path of the object across the sky, with the moments each picture was taken
obj.path_caption: Line: predicted path. Dots: where it was in each picture, colored by picture color (placed along the path).
inj.lede: We hid pretend asteroids in real pictures, then checked whether our search found them. Pick a size and a distance.
inj.grid_caption: Share of pretend asteroids found, by size (rows) and distance from the Sun (columns; 1 AU = the Earth–Sun distance). Pick a cell.
inj.yes: Yes: a {size} object at {r} AU from the Sun was usually found.
inj.no: No: a {size} object at {r} AU from the Sun was usually missed.
inj.alt_before: One picture with a planted pretend asteroid
inj.alt_after: {n} pictures combined along the planted object's path
inj.model_summary: How bright should it be? A simple estimate
inj.model_text: Sunlight reflected, seen face-on with the Sun behind us: V ≈ {V}.
inj.model_caveat: Assumes the object is seen exactly opposite the Sun and ignores its own heat glow. It explains the trend; the planted tests are what count.
live.form_hint: Type a position, or pick a famous target. We fetch the real pictures of that patch straight from the telescope's public archive and play them like a little video.
live.bad_coords: Please enter both coordinates, in degrees or as 08h55m10.8s / -07d14m42s.
live.note_epoch: {name}: catalogue position {ra}°, {dec}° (epoch 2000, SIMBAD). It has moved {moved}″ since then, so we centre on where it should be on {date}, the middle of the pictures we have.
live.note_barnard: The fastest-moving star in our sky: about 10.4″ per year, close to 1.7 pixels per year. The pink ring marks where the catalogue predicts it at each picture's time.
live.note_epsind: Two brown dwarfs, too close together to separate with 6.2″ pixels. Their star, Epsilon Indi A, is about 7′ west, outside even the 8′ view. The pink ring marks the predicted position.
live.note_wise: The coldest known brown dwarf, moving about 8.1″ per year. It is very faint at short wavelengths, so look at detectors 4–6. The challenge's coordinates (08h55m10.831s −07°14′42.53″) date from its 2010 detection; it has moved about 2′ since.
live.note_variable: A variable star: watch its brightness, not its position. Use Corrected to separate real brightness change from colour.
live.searching: Finding pictures that cover this position…
live.done: {n} pictures ({failed} failed) · {mb} MB · first picture after {first} s · all after {total} s
live.none: None of the {n} indexed pictures (taken {a} to {b}) covers this position yet. The index grows as more of the archive is processed.
live.no_index: The picture index is not available, so live mode cannot run.
live.error: Could not reach the telescope archive ({msg}). Check your connection and try again; the ready-made fields still work.
live.all_failed: Every download failed. The archive may be unreachable from this network.
live.canvas_aria: The current picture of this patch. Click a pixel to measure its spectrum.
live.corrected_wait: Corrected view becomes available once all pictures are in.
live.keys: Keys: space play/pause · ← → step · C raw/corrected
live.markers: Yellow ticks: the position you entered. Pink ring: predicted path of a fast-moving target. Blue square: pixel you clicked. Catalogue overlays (Gaia, WISE) are not shown: their services cannot be read directly by a browser.
live.add_hint: Adding pictures from the same detector lowers the noise. Each detector covers its own range of colours.
live.sub_hint: Pass 1 ({a} to {b}, {n1} pictures) minus pass 2 ({c} to {d}, {n2} pictures), split at the largest gap ({gap} days), using corrected pictures. A moving star shows as an orange–blue pair.
live.sub_short: The largest gap is shorter than two months, so these are not two separate sky surveys yet; slow movers will barely show.
live.sub_none: Need pictures on both sides of a time gap.
live.changes: plain blink, all pictures in time order: {all} changes; plain blink within each detector: {det}; after correction: {corr}.
live.spec_hint: Click or tap any pixel in the picture above.
live.spec_label: Quick aperture photometry (DATA, not the full model)
live.spec_where: Pixel ({i}, {j}), {dx}″ east and {dy}″ north of centre.
live.spec_title: Brightness against colour from {n} pictures near {ra}°, {dec}°
live.spec_none: No usable pictures at this pixel.
live.spec_caveat: 3×3-pixel sum minus the median of a ring 3–5 pixels out, converted with each picture's pixel solid angle. Error bars come from the ring's scatter and ignore the correlated noise added by resampling. Colours: pass 1 and pass 2.
live.changes_method: A change is a group of at least 2 pixels more than 5 noise units away from expected. Noise includes a {f} × brightness floor for imperfect star shapes. Single-pixel spikes are removed with a 3×3 median test, because live mode does not read the pixel-flag plane.
live.provisional: The {f} floor is provisional until it is measured on the calibration field.
live.subset: Showing {n} of {N} pictures, spread evenly in time.
finding.all_fields: Across all {n} fields, including the target stars: {pct}% of plain-blink changes removed ({naive} → {corr}).
